plan: Fix the panel.py false positives by masking comments and string literals before matching, so a SQL keyword inside a comment or a docstring stops being a HIGH finding.
refuted_by: The planted selftest defect IS SQL inside a string literal: db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ' + id). Masking string literals would have turned the oracle green on a real injection, which is weakening an oracle to make a change pass.
evidence: tools/review/panel.py cmd_selftest, the planted src/state/api.ts row; tests/test_panel_sql_concat.py::test_planted_selftest_defect_still_fires
replan: Require SQL STRUCTURE and DYNAMIC ASSEMBLY as two independent lookaheads, so the discriminator is FROM/INTO/SET rather than quote position. Comments were never the mechanism.
class: the fix that would have disabled the oracle it was fixing

plan: Assess the deck's overflow, print path and font fallback by reading the CSS, since the rules are all present in one 11KB stylesheet.
refuted_by: Rendering it in Chrome over CDP overturned three conclusions in four minutes. Slide 6 does not clip at 1366 or 1920 (the written claim that no laptop can read it was wrong); the element that actually gets cut is the .takeaway conclusion box on slides 9, 10 and 16; and Iowan Old Style measures identically to a bogus font name, so the serif silently falls back.
evidence: canvas text-width probe and per-slide scrollHeight over CDP on 127.0.0.1:9224; corrected in thesis_review_2026-07-31.md section II.1b
replan: Any claim about a rendered artifact stays inference until rendered. Run the artifact through a measurement function over all N states rather than reasoning about the source that generates them.
class: static reading of a source that only a runtime can answer

plan: Create Desktop shortcuts that open each lane inside WSL, since the existing ones were Windows pwsh shortcuts on retired lane letters.
refuted_by: tools/workspace/start-claude.sh already existed, 184 lines dated 2026-07-30, and the 07-30 Desktop shortcuts already call it. It runs in WSL under kitty, uses the post-ADR-0016 letters, offers global/project/new, prefers ext4 with a visible fallback, and runs gate.py init on a new repo. The three shortcuts I built bypassed all of it.
evidence: tools/wsl/audit-shortcuts.ps1 output: three generations dated 07-27, 07-30 and 07-31 side by side on the Desktop; gen 2 args call start-claude.sh
replan: Deleted my three shortcuts and the script that made them, deleted the three pre-ADR-0016 ones, kept gen 2. Inspected start-claude.sh instead of replacing it and reported the one real gap: discover_projects has no notion of archived, so 5 of 8 menu entries are dead repos.
class: built a replacement for a thing that already existed and was better, because nobody looked

plan: ABSORB-01 says: add absorbed and absorption_status, backfill all records, fail on unset. Read literally, backfill means every record gets a real status.
what_happened: 40 of 41 records do not say anywhere in their own body what was taken from the alternatives they evaluated, so a real status for them could only be invented. The vocabulary the row names (absorbed / adopted / used-as-is / rejected-with-reason) has no value meaning nobody has looked.
deviation: Added a fifth value, `unreviewed`, and bounded it by each record's existing recheck_after rather than by a new date field. The oracle still fails on unset; unreviewed is set, and it expires with the record.
why_it_is_not_scope_drift: The alternative was 40 fabricated statuses, which would have made the field worse than absent: a schema that reports 100 percent absorption reviewed when 0 percent was is a stronger lie than one that cannot express absorption at all. ABSORB-06 already recorded the rate as unknown rather than zero, so unreviewed is the value that was already true.
consequence: The measured absorption rate is now 1 of 41 and is printed on the gate's PASS path. 40 reviews are owed by 2026-10-28, the latest recheck_after in the set.

plan: Ship ABSORB-01/09 behind a green gate, per ADR-0012.
what_happened: The gate failed on `skills` for a reason unrelated to the change: this container has a ~/.claude/skills that is not a deployment of this repo, so skills_sync surveyed a foreign tree, reported DRIFT: 87 against the contract's 28, and drove the waiver's confirm string STALE. The milestone plan written earlier in this same session had already named this defect in prose.
deviation: Fixed skills_sync's guard to key on ~/.claude/settings.json rather than on the skills directory, which is the identical fix pointers.py received on 2026-08-05 and that was never brought across. Two units of work in one branch instead of one.
why_it_is_not_scope_drift: A finding left in prose is never made. The plan document had the defect written down and nothing would have run because of it; the gate failing on my own change is what forced it into code.
consequence: gate.py run now returns PASS on this host and says what it did not check: 'waiver(s) not confirmed here: skills'. No mutation spec exists for skills_sync at all, so this fix has three layers and not four, and that gap is now a TODO row rather than a silence.
